statement: Measured by running the tool against itself. It supports the claims it makes about itself (offline, read-only, no secret leakage, deterministic, fail-closed gate). It is not a certification of any deployment, and it does not replace independent third-party review.

sections.title: Automated test suite
sections.summary: The repository test suite executed as a child process; counts are parsed from its TAP output.

sections.title: Rule accuracy on the labelled corpus
sections.summary: 50 author-labelled cases. This is a regression corpus, not an independent benchmark: it shows the rules do what they claim on these inputs, not that they catch every real misconfiguration.

rows: Every per-document rule has a positive case
a resource missing from AFTER is reported

sections.title: Secret and state leakage
sections.summary: Canary strings were planted in every place a secret could plausibly be copied from, then the produced reports were searched for them.

rows: Env password, Secret data and annotation token never reach report JSON
3 canaries planted in BEFORE and AFTER; 0 found
Plan variables, prior_state, values and addresses never reach plan summary
canaries in variables, prior_state, before/after and address; 0 found
Secret-like env literal is flagged without echoing the value
Diffs mark redacted fields as redacted
Discarded plan sections are named, not copied
Shipped example reports contain no token-shaped strings

bullets: No canary appeared in any output.

sections.title: Hostile and malformed input
sections.summary: Untrusted manifests are data. The parser must fail loudly, never skip, never hang.

rows: 15/15 hostile inputs rejected with an Error
400 nesting levels handled without a stack overflow
this OS user cannot create symlinks (Windows without Developer Mode); covered on Linux/macOS CI

sections.title: Evidence integrity and gate safety
sections.summary: SHA-256 seals are tamper evidence, not signatures. The gate has exactly two states.

rows: Equal inputs give an identical digest (deterministic)
Digest survives a JSON round trip
No input can produce a READY gate
50 corpus resources assessed with every rollback box ticked; gates seen: HUMAN_REVIEW_REQUIRED, BLOCKED

sections.title: Static safety review of the source
sections.summary: Regex scans of the shipped code. They prove absence of these patterns, not absence of every possible vulnerability.

rows: No subprocess APIs in shipped packages
child_process appears only in the audit runner itself (it runs the test suite and the CLI help)
Only the loopback report server listens on a socket
node:http and listen() appear only in packages/server/index.mjs
No token-shaped strings in the shipped source

sections.title: Performance budgets
sections.summary: Median of 5 runs on this machine. Budgets are deliberately loose guardrails against regressions, not benchmarks of other hardware.

sections.title: Package and instruction assets
sections.summary: Structural checks that the shipped package is internally consistent.

rows: Every skill declares what deterministic command/rule backs it
20 agent roles registered with files on disk

sections.title: Explicitly not run
sections.summary: Listed so nobody mistakes absence of a result for a pass.

rows: by design: needs credentials; never run automatically
MCP server verified with a scripted JSON-RPC client only
Native activation of skills in each IDE
skills are copied, not proven to be loaded by each host
Independent third-party benchmark of the rules
npm provenance only if published via CI; reports carry unkeyed checksums, not signatures
macOS / Windows results from this run
only win32 was measured here; see CI for the matrix

reproduce: npm ci --ignore-scripts   # no dependencies, so this only checks the lockfile-free install
limits: Counts and timings come from this run on this machine.
The labelled corpus is written by the tool author; it is a regression corpus, not an independent benchmark.
Static rules inspect desired state only; they cannot prove runtime reachability, IAM scope or data recoverability.
A SHA-256 seal detects accidental or deliberate edits only when compared with a trusted copy; it does not authenticate the author.
Skill and agent files are instruction text; native activation in each IDE is untested.

integrity.meaning: Unkeyed integrity checksum, NOT a signature or proof of authenticity
